content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes (e.g., 76+), then sharply drop below true values.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts overshoot recent highs and fail to capture gradual downward drift.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) often underestimate true values, suggesting lag in adjusting to recent price trends.
- Model underreacts to sustained downward momentum; fails to reduce forecast when history shows clear downward trend.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the middle of the 30d window, especially when true values are trending lower.
- Model does not adjust for recent low prices; tends to maintain high forecasts even when history shows price consolidation or decline.
- Overshoots after spikes are followed by a sharp correction, but model fails to anticipate the magnitude of the drop.
- Model underestimates the persistence of recent lows; often fails to recognize that low prices can stay for multiple days.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30d history includes recent price consolidation or low volatility periods.
